anchor.quote: Each gate and each terminal $v$ of a network with frames carries a frame $D_v$, an invertible operator on arrays.

anchor.note: Only the plain symbol g is bound on an earlier page, as the logical array. Nothing says what the subscripted g_1 denotes, such as the first of two arrays.
Only the plain symbol g is bound on an earlier page, as the logical array. Nothing says what the subscripted g_2 denotes, such as the second of two arrays.

gaps.quote: A pointwise linear gate commutes with its frame
gaps.note: The term is used as a known class of gate, but the page only defines a scalar gate acting at each address and does not say what makes a gate pointwise linear, nor link to a page that does.

gaps.quote: For a two-wire gate this reads
gaps.note: The reader is asked to accept G(D_v g_1, D_v g_2) = D_v G(g_1, g_2) without a reason. The page does not show why applying the frame before or after a pointwise gate gives the same result, so the reader cannot check it from the page.

gaps.quote: replace two wire values by their sum and then by their difference
gaps.note: The page does not say which value is subtracted from which, or whether the sum and difference are both taken from the original values. The reader cannot check that the stated results 4 and 2 follow from the description.
